To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pseudo-language strategy is the most effective for an introduction to imperative-procedural programming; that the sequence of imperative-procedural followed by object-oriented programming is the most appropriate for teaching programming in general; that the difficulties that programming students face are not language-specific; that a successful teaching design for programming courses is one based on a problem-solving approach; and that students rely mainly on the instructor for learning programming.

a pseudo-language can be a very effective tool for introducing non-CS majors to programming, that students have difficulties learning imperative-procedural programming but not object-oriented programming, that students need to have a solid understanding of imperative-procedural before learning object-oriented programming, and that the teaching and learning process of programming can be improved by using a variety of teaching and learning techniques and materials.

a pseudo-language is a very good choice for an introductory programming course; the transition from procedural programming to object-oriented programming is a difficult task; and the teaching and learning of programming is a difficult process.
